surprises: AMGT_RESAPP-Z-W1-S1: AMGT-s-12's universe.json carries a measurement defect -- 16 of its 48 MEASURED bloomberg_ticker values, across unrelated folders including the CRO's own control folder SAP GY, all read the identical string 'AAPL US'. select_securities.py excludes every duplicate-valued entry before picking a US-domiciled name and an ADR, so the defect did not propagate into this order's three securities (the control, SAP GY Equity, is taken directly from the task order text/CRO brief, never from this universe.json row). Not fixed here -- outside this worker's <paths> grant, and a different cell's deliverable.

AMGT_RESAPP-Z-W1-S2: for the ADR (BABA US Equity, fiscal year end 31 March), Bloomberg's raw historical response never carries a single row with both a price field and a fundamentals field -- 100% of its rows split fiscal-period-end (March) fundamentals from calendar-year-end (December) price/ratios. Grouping by the calendar year of `date` (this order's fiscal-year join rule) satisfies AC4's row-count and orphan-count bar exactly (10 FY rows, 0 orphans, same as the other two securities) but, for this specific security, merges each fiscal year's fundamentals with a price observation roughly nine months later rather than one at the fiscal period end. A self-consistent check (Bloomberg's own PE_RATIO vs a naive PX_LAST/IS_EPS computed from the same fiscal-year-merged group) reconciles to 6 decimal places on the control (December FYE) and disagrees by a factor of ~5.9x on BABA -- consistent with a currency difference, the ~9-month timing gap, an ADR share-ratio effect, or some combination; not isolated to one cause, and not reconciled further (bound (f): state the finding, never guess past what was measured).
